Under the trunk floor mat of his German-registered Mazda, customs officers found 18.566 kg of hashish and 996.7 g of cocaine. The man admitted smuggling the hashish but denied knowing the cocaine was in the car. Agder district court sentenced him to 4 years in prison in August 2026. The court also noted he had the opportunity to contact police before crossing the border and was to receive an economic benefit. The final sentence of 2 years includes credit for 374 days the man had already served in pre-trial detention.

cases.title: South Africa legalises private cannabis use
cases.why: A change in the law (the Cannabis for Private Purposes Act, signed in May 2024). Law changes go to the Cannabis Freedom Index history, not into the tracker.

attempts.decision_title: South Africa cannabis law change
attempts.explanation: This report concerns the Cannabis for Private Purposes Act signed into law by President Cyril Ramaphosa on May 27, 2024, making South Africa the first African nation to legalise recreational cannabis use. As this is a law change rather than an enforcement event, it belongs in the Cannabis Freedom Index history, not the tracker. The article reports on the legislative change, its background, implications, and context within African drug policy reform, including historical use of cannabis (dagga) in South Africa, the 2018 Constitutional Court ruling, the six-year legislative process, and reactions from activists, policymakers, and other African nations.
